payload.claim: review_commit_diff builds its returned diff text with a plain `git diff --literal-pathspecs ... diff ...` call that does not set `-c core.quotePath=false`, unlike the `git_mirror.changed_files` calls just above it (lines 146-147) that do set it. For a changed path outside plain ASCII, git octal-escapes the `diff --git a/... b/...` header by default, and `saffron/gates/core/integrity.py`'s `_parse_block` then returns that escaped literal string as the path rather than the real filename (confirmed by `_FILE_HEADER`'s quoted-path branch, which captures the raw escaped text). `own_version_pairs` feeds this returned diff straight into `_changed_paths`, so for a witness whose file has a non-ASCII name, the path comparison in `_chosen_criteria` silently fails to match, and that criterion's already-killed wrong version is never re-asked, with no error and no signal that anything was skipped. The repository's own fixtures and tests use only ASCII test paths, so this gap would not show up there but would in a repo with a non-ASCII witness filename.
